title: Endgame Ring & Amulet Crafting Guide for Attack Builds | PoE 2 0.5 Runes of Aldur
creator: Alohaa

base.name: Breach Ring
base.quote: you want to start with an breach ring, preferably item level 82 because item level 82 can roll tier one max res.

target.text: T1 flat damage to attacks (fire, cold, lightning or physical; physical least preferred)

steps.quote: I like to annul and roll until you hit one of the tier one modifiers with damage to attacks, either fire, cold, lightning, or fizz.
steps.note: He says 'annul and roll' without naming the roll orb; chaos is inferred from the later chaos spamming (1:37).

target.text: two more modifiers so the ring has three mods to fracture from

steps.quote: I'll add a greater exaltation omen with a greater exalted to add two modifiers.

target.text: a desecrated mod, which cannot be fractured, so the fracture hits only the other mods

steps.quote: you want to make sure that you have added a desecrated modifier. a desecrated modifier cannot be fractured.
steps.note: Bone, side and omens for this protective desecration are not stated.

target.text: fracture the T1 flat damage to attacks

steps.quote: I have three mods right here and if I use a fracturing orb, I have a one in three chance to hit.

target.text: second T1 flat damage to attacks

steps.quote: keep chaos spamming until you hit another tier one to attacks. This takes about, I think, roughly 200 to 300 chaos on average
steps.note: How the two mods are removed is not stated.

steps.quote: I use an omen of dextra exaltation. This will make it that your next exalted orb is only adding one suffix.
This essence is guaranteed to remove your suffix modifier and adds 20% maximum quality to your ring.
steps.note: Ring then has three prefixes: two T1 attack flats and the quality mod (2:23–2:27).

target.text: two suffixes: lightning resistance and all-resistances most likely

steps.quote: I'm using a greater exaltation to add two suffix modifiers and a perfect exaltation to add high tier of these two suffix modifiers.
steps.note: Applies 60% lightning catalyst quality first (2:36–2:39), which the Catalysing omen consumes. He hit all-res and physical attack damage leeched as mana, both suffixes (3:37–3:40, 4:32–4:55); the caption's 'tier one physical damage to attacks' at 3:18–3:21 is that leech suffix (item level 38), not a prefix flat.

target.text: Attack-modifier quality (60%) restored before removing the quality mod

steps.quote: I have to apply the reaver catalyst because there's no way to remove the physical damage as mana with a whitling orb.
steps.note: Applied before the whittle so quality survives.

target.text: remove the quality mod, then keep whittling until good suffixes land (T1 res preferred)

steps.quote: An omen of whittling will remove the lowest tier modifier and add a new modifier via a chaos orb.
steps.note: He uses a greater chaos orb here and a plain chaos orb at 5:20. Whittling targets the lowest item-level mod (physical attack damage as mana is level 38, life 54, attack flats 75; 4:51–5:16).

target.text: last prefix: another T1 damage to attacks

steps.quote: use echoings with color bones in order to reveal another tier one damage to attacks. And if it doesn't work
steps.note: 'Echoings' is Omen of Abyssal Echoes; 'omen of blight' removes the desecrated mod, so Omen of Light is meant. 'Color bones' is a collarbone, type not stated. He says finish the desecration before whittling more (6:10–6:15).

missHandling.trigger: whittle lands a poor suffix (T2 dexterity, then life is the next lowest-level mod)
missHandling.quote: the next whittling is going to remove the max life. you just have a life as the next tier modifier, next lowest tier modifier

missHandling.trigger: revealed mod is not a T1 flat to attacks
missHandling.quote: if it doesn't work, you can use an omen of blight to remove the desecrated modifier and go again until you hit tier one attacks.
missHandling.note: Omen of Light to remove the desecrated mod, then a new bone.

qualityPath.orderNote: Lightning catalyst to 60% for the catalysed resistance slam (consumed); then Attack catalyst back to 60% before whittling the Breach quality mod, because the quality stays after the mod is removed.

measured.context: chance per chaos of a second T1 flat, derived from 'roughly 200 to 300 chaos on average'
measured.quote: This takes about, I think, roughly 200 to 300 chaos on average, so be prepared.

measured.context: fracturing orb on a three-mod ring
measured.quote: I have three mods right here and if I use a fracturing orb, I have a one in three chance to hit.

claims.text: recommended minimum bankroll: 200 div for the ring craft
claims.quote: if you do not have 200 divines to spare for this craft, I do not recommend starting it.

claims.text: chaos spam for the second T1 flat: 200 to 300 chaos on average
finished ring worth about 200 to 600 div
claims.quote: the ring is probably worth around anywhere between 200 to maybe 600 divines or 500 divines.

caveats: The last desecration is described as one of the most expensive parts, up to hundreds of div if unlucky (6:34–6:38); no number given.
The video also covers a gold amulet craft (6:52–11:22, about 100 div, 10:57 onward); not extracted, it is not a ring.
He claims it is cheaper to craft the ring than to buy one (6:47–6:51).
unresolved: Fracture odds: he says one in three with three mods while one of them is desecrated and unfracturable, which would leave two eligible; how many mods the ring held is unclear (1:19–1:33).
Bone type, side and omens for the protective desecration at step 3 are not stated.
How the two mods are removed before the second chaos spam (1:35) is not stated.
Final ring state and cost of his own ring are not shown.
